notes: Commercial Terms incorporate the DPA and forbid training on customer content; first-party API offers only 'us'/'global' inference geo (EU only via Bedrock/Vertex); not on DPF list.
The Apple Developer Program License Agreement contains no processor/DPA terms for APNs, Sign in with Apple or App Store Connect; Apple offers none.
AWS DPA is part of the AWS Service Terms and SCCs apply automatically; Amazon Web Services, Inc. is a covered entity under Amazon.com's active DPF certification.

Microsoft Products and Services DPA governs Azure subscriptions; Speech processes data only in the resource's region and EU regions fall under the EU Data Boundary; Microsoft DPF 'Active - re-certification under review'.
DPA supplements the ToS and customers are deemed to have agreed to SCCs; Backblaze is active on DPF and offers an EU Central region (must be picked at account creation).

action: No public DPA; request via Contact Sales (enterprise contract) or privacy@blackforestlabs.ai
notes: Standard FLUX API terms have no DPA and grant BFL rights to use inputs/outputs incl. model training; only enterprise-contract data is treated as processed on behalf of customers (EEA entity: BFL GmbH, Freiburg).

Brave's DPA (referenced by the API ToS) explicitly excludes Search Query Data and states Brave is not a processor for it; DPA otherwise relies on EU SCCs; Brave Software not found on DPF list; query logs kept up to 90 days unless enterprise ZDR.

action: Log in to the bunny.net dashboard (panel) and complete the Data Processing Agreement there.
notes: BunnyWay d.o.o. is in Ljubljana, Slovenia; CDN edges are global, so EU-only routing/storage regions must be chosen deliberately.
Self-Serve Subscription Agreement §6.1 incorporates the DPA by reference; R2 supports EU jurisdiction buckets but CDN/DNS process globally; DPF status 'Active - re-certification under review'.

Complimenta is the clinic's processor under the clinic's own DPA, not ours; our API access happens on the clinic's behalf, so we need a DPA with the clinic. Their privacy page still cites Privacy Shield/model clauses.

action: Request and sign via help@daily.co (per https://www.daily.co/security/gdpr-compliance/)
notes: The DPA says primary processing is in the US and transfers go via DPF with SCC fallback; DPF listing not independently verified.
Free Danish government address data (Grunddataprogrammet); only the lookup query is sent.

action: No public DPA found; ask policy@deepinfra.com or trust.deepinfra.com (portal returned 403)
notes: Privacy policy says data is processed in the United States; no DPA on public pages; not on DPF list; states it does not store or train on API inputs.

DeepL SE (Cologne). The DPA (in DeepL's Trust Centre) is part of the Pro terms and binds when you subscribe. The free API ('DeepL API Developer') forbids personal data, so a paid plan is required; DeepL chooses where data is processed.
China-based (Hangzhou DeepSeek), PRC law governs, no DPA or processor terms offered; not suitable for personal data.
Discord's processor DPA only covers partner products such as Custom Audiences, so for plain webhooks Discord acts as its own controller; Discord, Inc. is active on DPF.
DPA applies automatically to self-serve (Terms); EU data residency is Enterprise-only via a separate isolated environment.
The DPA is incorporated into the online terms and uses SCCs (DPF only if fal later notifies it); the privacy policy makes no DPF claim.
Firebase Data Processing and Security Terms are incorporated into the Firebase terms and explicitly cover Cloud Messaging; data may be processed wherever Google has facilities.

Clause 8 of the Master Terms (https://flexprice.io/msa) is the DPA; Indian company (Squirrelly Technologies Pvt Ltd) processing in India/US with no named transfer mechanism, and India has no EU adequacy decision.

action: Sign in → Documents (fly.io/documents) → sign the DPA (pre-signed by Fly.io, active once customer signs)
notes: Fly.io is active on EU-US/UK/Swiss DPF; DPA not in effect until the customer signs it in the dashboard.
DPA supplements the ToS with SCC Modules 2/3 deemed signed; Delaware (US) company not found on DPF list, subprocessors in US/UK.

action: DPA takes effect on both parties' signature; how to sign isn't stated online, so check the GatewayAPI dashboard or ask support
notes: Danish (OnlineCity, Odense); sub-processors are Hetzner (DE/FI) and HeySender (DK), with an EU setup option; GatewayAPI acts as controller for the messaging itself and processor for the 30-day traffic log.
DPA forms part of the GitHub Customer Agreement for Online Services (previews excluded); in-region storage only if you use a service offering a specific geographic area.

CDPA is incorporated into Google Cloud terms (Vertex); Gemini API Paid Services use Google's processor DPA and no training, and EEA-facing apps must use Paid Services; Google LLC active on DPF (SCC appendix not verified).

For businesses established in the EEA the Google Ads Data Processing Terms (https://business.safety.google/adsprocessorterms/, which list Google Analytics) are already incorporated; Google LLC is active on DPF; GA4 still widely challenged by EU DPAs.
Google acts as independent controller for Maps Platform under the Controller-Controller Data Protection Terms (https://business.safety.google/controllerterms/), which use SCCs/DPF.
The DDA says using Play means accepting Google's controller-to-controller data protection terms, so Google is its own controller, not our processor; transfers use SCCs.
The API only takes a public URL to analyse, so no personal data is sent; no DPA is offered.

action: Admin console (super admin) → Menu → Account → Account settings → Legal and compliance → Security and Privacy Additional Terms → Cloud Data Processing Addendum → Review and Accept
notes: Google says opt-in is only needed if your agreement doesn't already incorporate the CDPA (https://cloud.google.com/terms/data-processing-addendum), and accepting is harmless if it does; Google OAuth login is identity only.

Gravatar is covered by Automattic's privacy policy with Aut O'Mattic A8C Ireland Ltd as controller for EU users; no Gravatar DPA found; Automattic Inc. is active on DPF, and visitor IPs reach US servers when images load.

action: In Hetzner account go to https://accounts.hetzner.com/account/dpa, fill data types + data subject categories (Appendix 1) and tick 'I agree to the agreement'.
notes: Without a concluded DPA Hetzner assumes no third-party personal data is processed; cloud data stays where the chosen location is (avoid US/Singapore locations).

action: Get an Enterprise Hub or Enterprise plan (huggingface.co/enterprise); the GDPR DPA is offered only through that subscription.
notes: Downloading public models sends no personal data, so no DPA is needed for that part. Inference with personal data needs the Enterprise DPA, which uses SCCs.

action: Existing customers: find/accept the data processing agreement in the inMobile account; otherwise order it via the 'Order Data Processing Agreement & ISAE 3000' form on that page.
notes: Danish provider hosting exclusively in EU data centres with ISAE 3000 type 2 report from Deloitte.
For Sign In with LinkedIn, LinkedIn is the identity provider; the API Terms still automatically incorporate the BD DPA (controller-to-controller or processor modules, SCCs, Irish law).

DPA forms part of the ToS; DPF first with SCCs as fallback. Region pinning covers media only; observability and inference data may leave the pinned region. DPF status comes from LiveKit's privacy policy (the DPF list page could not be read).
French company, data hosted in EU by default; API inputs/outputs are used for training by default unless opted out (Admin panel → Privacy toggle).
The GDPR page says the DPA (PDF at netlify.com/pdf/netlify-dpa.pdf) is incorporated into the terms. Functions default to us-east-2 and can be set to eu-central-1.
Only public package publishing; npm's privacy page mentions no DPA covering npm (the GitHub DPA covers GitHub Online Services).

DPA is incorporated into the Services Agreement (EEA customers contract with OpenAI Ireland); a signed copy can also be executed via OpenAI's DPA form; not on DPF list; EU data residency only for sales-approved eligible customers on new projects.

Terms §10.2 incorporates the DPA for commercial users (help article says countersigned DPA is enterprise-only); EU-only processing requires the EU API via an enterprise Order Form; upstream model providers are separate sub-processors; not on DPF list.
Public subtitle lookup with an app API key and no personal data sent; the vendor's pages returned 403, so its terms could not be read.

action: No public DPA document; request it from hej@opkald.ai
notes: Danish service; its site says it works as data processor with a databehandleraftale and stores data in the EU.

action: No public DPA found; request one from pCloud via https://www.pcloud.com/contact or privacy@pcloud.com
notes: Swiss entity (pCloud International AG); the Business Agreement has no Art. 28 DPA; the EU data region is Luxembourg and is chosen at signup.

DPA page returned 403 to our fetch; per search-indexed text the DPA is incorporated into the API Terms and uses SCC Modules 2/3, Perplexity AI is active on DPF, and API infra is AWS North America with zero-day prompt retention.

action: Download the Piwik PRO data processing clauses, sign and return countersigned copy to legal+dpa@piwik.pro (clauses take effect on both parties' signature).
notes: Piwik PRO SA is in Wroclaw, Poland; default cloud hosting is Elastx in Sweden, with US/HK hosting options that must be avoided.

DPA forms part of the Polar Master Services Terms with SCC Module 2; Polar Software, Inc. (San Francisco) not found on DPF list, and as Merchant of Record Polar may be an independent controller for buyer checkout data.

action: Download the QuickPay DPA PDF, fill in our company details, sign and return to QuickPay (the agreement becomes effective on signing).
notes: QuickPay ApS (DK-21822434), Danish law; the helpdesk article that linked the DPA now 404s so return path is not documented.

action: Email sales@requesty.ai with company name + signatory contact; they send the standard Art. 28 DPA for e-signature. Zero Data Retention also only on written request.
notes: EU gateway in Frankfurt can keep the full request path in the EU; DPA page names no transfer mechanism and Requesty Ltd is not on the DPF list.
eu-west-1 only changes the sending region; all account data, logs and metadata are stored in the US; DPF 'Active - re-certification under review'.

action: Fill in the signature block and required information in the DPA and submit it via the link on the DPA page; it binds only after that.
notes: Special-category data (incl. health) is barred. EU data centers can be chosen (e.g. EU-SE-1, EU-RO-1), but the DPA gives no hard EU residency guarantee.

DPA (June 2024) forms an integral part of the Scaleway services contract; services are located in the EU by default and region is chosen at order time; linked from https://www.scaleway.com/en/contracts/.

action: Simply.com Kontrolpanel (logged in) → find the databehandleraftale and sign it there
notes: Danish company with a fixed standard DPA they won't modify; must be signed in the control panel; hosting location isn't stated on the page.

action: Have an authorised signatory execute the DPA via the link on slack.com/terms-of-service/data-processing (available on all plans).
notes: Salesforce (Slack) is active on DPF and the DPA includes SCCs; EU data residency exists only on paid plans.

action: Log in at SMS.dk, open the personal menu, choose 'GDPR' and enter the standard databehandleraftale.
notes: Run by Compaya A/S; the page says data is hosted in Denmark.
DPA forms part of the Stripe agreement; EEA accounts contract with Stripe Payments Europe Ltd (Ireland) but data may be transferred globally.
Public subtitle lookup with no personal data sent; subdl.com/terms returned 403, and commercial API use requires an active paid plan (per a search snippet).
DPA says acceptance of the Agreement has the same effect as signing the SCCs; not on DPF list; EU regions incl. Stockholm eu-north-1 and Frankfurt.
The DPA is incorporated by reference for business use and relies on SCCs, with no DPF mention. Data is processed in Canada, Germany, the US and the UK, with no EU residency option.

action: Request the DPA from support@tavily.com (per Tavily Trust Center); not published publicly.
notes: US company (AlphaAI Technologies Inc.), not on DPF list; ToS lets Tavily and its AI providers use customer input for model training, and privacy policy says SCC protections apply to enterprise subscribers.
Service Agreement §22.3 incorporates the DPA; SCC Module 2/3 in DPA; not on DPF list; EU-only possible via eur multi-region or fra+ams dual-region buckets (default is global).
The API terms contain no DPA or GDPR clauses; this is a public metadata lookup where we only send an API key.

action: Log in → Documents section → execute the Data Processing Agreement (paid subscribers only; blog says Scaler/Pro/Enterprise)
notes: DPA only on paid plans and must be executed manually; not on DPF list; EU location aws-eu-west-1 (Ireland) available.
The DPA is deemed signed when you accept Twilio's terms; transfers use DPF, then BCRs, then SCCs; the Ireland (IE1) region exists but not every product is available there.
The API terms name the developer an independent controller. The required hotlinking lets Unsplash see end-user IPs and image views, which belongs in the privacy notice.

action: Upgrade to a Pro or Enterprise plan. The DPA applies automatically there; Hobby (free) has no DPA.
notes: The DPA text uses SCCs; the DPF certification comes from Vercel's changelog. Functions default to iad1 (US) and must be set to an EU region such as fra1 or cdg1.

Section 10 ('Data Processing Terms') is built into the T&C. Data is stored in the EEA, with transfers only exceptionally under SCCs plus advance notice; sub-processors at trust.verda.com/subprocessors.

action: DPA only on Enterprise/OTT plans (https://vimeo.com/legal/enterprise-terms/dpa); self-serve plans get none, but embed users can sign controller-to-controller SCCs via Vimeo's webform (https://www.vimeo.axdraft.com).
notes: Vimeo.com, Inc. is active on DPF; self-serve accounts have no DPA.
Browser push services only relay payloads end-to-end encrypted to the browser with a per-site anonymous identifier; no vendor DPA exists (Chrome goes via FCM, Safari via Apple).

Zoom's trust page (https://www.zoom.com/en/trust/gdpr/) says the DPA is incorporated into the Terms of Service; DPF participant since 10 Jul 2023; EU data-centre regions only on eligible paid accounts.
